title: Module Documentation: Prime Classification by p+1 Factorization
content: Erdős Problem #1055: classify primes by the factorization depth of $p+1$. Class 1 primes have 3-smooth $p+1$. Class $r$ primes: all prime factors of $p+1$ are in class $\leq r-1$, with at least one in class $r-1$. Key questions: infinitely many in each class? Growth of $p_r^{1/r}$ (Erdős: $\to \infty$; Selfridge: bounded). Known: $p_1=2, p_2=13, p_3=37, p_4=73, p_5=1021$ (OEIS A005113).
mathContext: $\text{primeClass}(p) = 1 + \max\{\text{primeClass}(q) : q \mid (p+1),\, q \text{ prime}\}$ with base case $\text{primeClass}(2) = \text{primeClass}(3) = 1$.

title: Foldl Max Helper Lemmas
content: Two private helpers for `List.foldl max`: `foldl_max_ge_init` (fold $\geq$ init) and `foldl_max_ge_of_mem` ($x \in l \Rightarrow$ fold $\geq f(x)$). Both use term-mode structural induction. These establish correctness of the prime class computation via `foldl max` over prime factors.

title: Termination Lemma: nonSmooth_factor_lt
content: The key lemma enabling well-founded recursion for `primeClass`: any prime factor $q$ of $p+1$ with $q \notin \{2,3\}$ satisfies $q < p$. The proof proceeds by contradiction: $q \leq p+1$ (since $q \mid p+1$), and $q = p$ is impossible (since $p \mid p+1$ implies $p \mid 1$), and $q = p+1$ is impossible (since $p+1$ being prime and even — because $p$ is odd — forces $p+1 = 2$, contradiction). This strict decrease $q < p$ is the termination argument: recursive calls to `primeClass q` always use a smaller input.
mathContext: If $p$ is prime and $q \mid (p+1)$ with $q \neq 2, 3$ and $q$ prime, then $q < p$. Proof: $q \leq p+1$; if $q = p$ then $p \mid (p+1)$ so $p \mid 1$, impossible; if $q = p+1$ then $p+1$ is prime but $2 \mid (p+1)$ (since $p$ is odd prime), so $p+1 = 2$, contradiction. Hence $q \leq p-1 < p$.

title: Prime Class Definition
content: The class of a prime p, defined recursively: class 1 means p+1 is 3-smooth; class r means all prime factors of p+1 have class ≤ r-1 with at least one at r-1. The `primeClass` function uses well-founded recursion on `q < p` (since prime factors of `p+1` are at most `p` for `p ≥ 2`). `IsInClass` is the combined predicate requiring both primality and matching class.
mathContext: The **Erdős–Selfridge prime classification** assigns to each prime $p$ a class $c(p) \in \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$ by recursion on the prime factorization of $p+1$. Formally: $c(p) = 1$ if $p+1$ is $3$-smooth (only factors $2$ and $3$), and $c(p) = 1 + \max\{c(q) : q \mid p+1, q \text{ prime}\}$ otherwise. The $+1$ shift means the classification probes the **multiplicative structure of shifted primes** $p + 1$, a central topic in analytic number theory.

title: Verified Class Values via native_decide
content: 20 computationally verified class assignments using `native_decide`. Class 1 primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 17, 23, 31 (all have $p+1 = 2^a \cdot 3^b$). Class 2: 13 ($14=2\cdot7$), 19 ($20=2^2\cdot5$), 29 ($30=2\cdot3\cdot5$), 41 ($42=2\cdot3\cdot7$), 43 ($44=2^2\cdot11$). Class 3: 37 ($38=2\cdot19$), 103 ($104=2^3\cdot13$), 113 ($114=2\cdot3\cdot19$). Class 4: 73 ($74=2\cdot37$). Class 5: 1021 ($1022=2\cdot7\cdot73$). Non-primes get class 0: verified for 4 and 6. All proofs are `by native_decide` — kernel computation of the recursive definition.
mathContext: Class 1 primes are those $p$ where $p + 1 = 2^a \cdot 3^b$: the **3-smooth shifted primes**. The chain structure: $13 \to 14 = 2 \cdot 7$ ($c(7) = 1$), $37 \to 38 = 2 \cdot 19$ ($c(19) = 2$), $73 \to 74 = 2 \cdot 37$ ($c(37) = 3$), $1021 \to 1022 = 2 \cdot 7 \cdot 73$ ($c(73) = 4$).

title: Least Prime in Each Class (OEIS A005113)
content: Defines `findLeastPrimeInClass` (bounded linear search) and verifies the first 5 values: $p_1=2$, $p_2=13$, $p_3=37$, $p_4=73$, $p_5=1021$. Each verified by `native_decide`. The values $p_r^{1/r}$: $2, 3.61, 3.33, 2.92, 4.01$ are tantalizingly inconclusive about the growth rate — they don't clearly trend upward (supporting Erdős) or stabilize (supporting Selfridge).
mathContext: The sequence of **least primes in each class** (OEIS A005113): $p_1 = 2$, $p_2 = 13$, $p_3 = 37$, $p_4 = 73$, $p_5 = 1021$. The $r$th roots $p_r^{1/r}$: $2.00, 3.61, 3.33, 2.92, 4.01$ — inconclusive between the Erdős ($\to \infty$) and Selfridge (bounded) conjectures.

title: Structural Properties and Concrete Evidence
content: Proved structural theorems: `primeClass_pos_of_prime` (primes have class $\geq 1$), `class_of_factor_lt` (if $q \mid p+1$ and $q$ prime, then $c(q) < c(p)$), `class_one_iff_smooth` (class 1 $\iff$ $p+1$ is 3-smooth). Also concrete evidence for infinitude: `many_class1_primes` ($\geq 8$ class-1 primes below 50), `many_class2_primes` ($\geq 8$ class-2 primes below 100), `many_class3_primes` ($\geq 3$ class-3 primes below 200). These are verified by `native_decide`.
mathContext: Key structural facts: $c(p) \geq 1$ for all primes $p$, $q \mid (p+1)$ prime $\Rightarrow c(q) < c(p)$ (strict decrease along factorization chains), and $c(p) = 1 \iff p + 1$ is 3-smooth. The concrete lists provide evidence for the infinitude conjecture.

title: The Main Conjectures (OPEN)
content: Four axiomatized conjectures: (1) `infinitely_many_in_each_class`: for each $r \geq 1$, infinitely many primes have class $r$ — the primary question. (2) `erdos_growth_conjecture`: $p_r^{1/r} \to \infty$ (superexponential growth of least class-$r$ prime). (3) `selfridge_bounded_conjecture`: $\exists C, \forall r, p_r \leq C^r$ (exponential growth). These are **mutually exclusive** — exactly one of Erdős and Selfridge is right. (4) `class_density_subpolynomial`: $|\{p \leq n : c(p) = r\}| = n^{o(1)}$ (extreme sparsity of each class).
mathContext: The central tension: Erdős predicted $p_r^{1/r} \to \infty$ (factorization chains force astronomical primes), while Selfridge predicted $p_r^{1/r}$ bounded (chains can be threaded efficiently). The density axiom $n^{o(1)}$ reflects the compounding sparsity of recursive smoothness constraints. All four conjectures remain OPEN.
